newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Violence a high point in Sri Lanka poll rhetoric.
newsitem.headline: Violence a high point in Sri Lanka poll rhetoric.

text.p: Sri Lanka's main political parties traded accusations on Friday over violence in the run-up to the country's local council elections next week.

The main opposition United National Party (UNP) complained its members were being harassed and threatened by supporters of the ruling People's Alliance (PA), headed by President Chandrika Kumaratunga.

"Our people are not moving about as they used to. We have stopped campaigning after dark because of threats," said P. Dayaratne, senior UNP legislator and chairman of the party's campaign coordinating committee.
"The safety of our members hangs in the balance as we go into the last few days of campaigning," Dayaratne told Reuters.
Alliance members countered that the UNP was lodging bogus complaints of violence against it to win voter sympathy.
"These are wild allegations. All we are doing is campaigning vigorously to win this election," government minister Mohamed Fowzie told Reuters.
"We will win more than 65 percent of the councils including Colombo and many of the big out-station ones," said Fowzie, who is the PA's chief campaign organiser for Colombo.
Campaigning for the March 21 poll ends at midnight on Tuesday.
The poll, the PA's first popularity test since it won power in 1994 seats in remote villages to 53 in Colombo.
The UNP coof a ruling coalition legislator last month.
An opposition UNP member of parliament and a former UNP mayor are among the suspects detained by police in connection with the killing.

The Centre for Monitoring Election Violence, an independent monitoring group, said about 1,000 incidents of polls-related violence have been reported since last month. The highest number of allegations were made against the alliance, it said.
On Friday, a Colombo judge ordered UNP lawmaker Pradeep Hapangama to be remanded till after the election for his alleged involvement in the shooting of a PA candidate.
A former leftist rebel group making its debut as a political party said its members also were being harassed, mostly by government supporters.
"We are an emerging political party and pose a threat to the government even more so than the UNP," said Wimal Weerawansa of the People's Liberation Front (JVP), which is fielding 3,800 candidates.
"Even if we don't win councils, we hope to win substantial representation in many of them," he said.

Nearly 20,000 candidates from 12 political parties and 132 independent groups are contesting 238 councils throughout the country except in the northern and eastern provinces, where separatist Tamil rebels are waging an independence war against the government.
Seats for councils in 12 cities, 31 towns and 195 villages will be up for election. The size of the councils range from nine seats in remote villages to 53 in Colombo.
The UNP controlled about 75 percent of the councils before they were dissolved in January.
